messages.content: what is different about there is a book on the table and it is on the table?
there is a book on the table says a book is there. it is on the table usually is about an object already known from context.
make that explanation shorter.
the first can bring a new book into the conversation. the other needs context to know what it is.
make a short conversation.
where is my book? it is on the table.
now one where i am just telling someone what i see.
there is a book on the table.
can it mean the table instead of the book?
context can make it about different things. in the short conversation about your book, it is the book.
only give the sentence with there again.
there is a book on the table.
write a longer story about a person keeping the right detail from a conversation. the note should be short but useful for a later task.

a woman talked with her brother about meeting after work. they spent a long time talking about books, food, and the way their week had gone. before finishing the call, she wrote only three details on a page: the day, the time, and the place they had chosen. the next afternoon, she remembered many parts of the conversation but was not sure which restaurant they had chosen. she looked at the page and found the place there. the note had not kept every word, but it had kept the parts she needed to meet him. when she came, he had his own small note with the same plan. they both had a laugh at how much they had talked and how little they needed written down for this task.
why did the short note help?
it kept the details needed for the meeting, even though it did not keep the whole conversation.
what were the three details?
the day, the time, and the place.
make that answer a full sentence about why the page helped.
she kept the chosen place on a page and used it to meet him the next day.
can a short note be useful without being the whole story?
yes. it can be enough for one task while leaving other parts out.
finish with them putting the pages away.
they checked that they had found each other and put the pages away. then they began a new conversation over tea.
can can be about knowing how and also about a choice being okay?
yes. i can read can be about knowing how. you can use this chair can say it is okay to sit there.
make that explanation shorter.
can can be about knowing how or about a choice being okay.
if someone asks can i sit here, what do they usually want?
they usually want to know whether using that place is okay, not whether their body can sit.
now give a kind yes.
yes, you can sit here.
what if the chair is for someone else?
you could say: sorry, someone else needs this chair. there is another one near the window.
can you know another chair is there?
not unless you tell me. without that detail, keep the answer to the chair you know about.
only give the no without another chair.
sorry, someone else needs this chair.
write one sentence with ten words about reading with my sister at home.
i read a book with my sister at home today.
now take today out. how many words are left?
nine words are left.
only give the shorter sentence.
i read a book with my sister at home.
add tomorrow instead, and make it about a plan.
i will read a book with my sister at home tomorrow.
is that still ten words?
no. it has ten words and one more, because will was added as well as tomorrow.
explain why it got longer.
today was taken out, but both will and tomorrow were added.
can you make a ten word plan by using books instead of a book?
i will read books with my sister at home tomorrow.
check that count before answering.
that sentence has ten words.
i did not finish the page today, but i understood one part that had been hard.
that is a change you can name even while the page is not finished.
i want to tell my teacher without saying i did everything.
you could say: i have not finished the page yet, but i understand this part better now.
can i add that i still need help with the last sentence?
i have not finished the page yet. i understand this part better, but i still need help with the last sentence.
why not just say i cannot do it?
because that leaves out the part you now understand. a more specific answer gives both what you can do and what still needs help.
only give the sentence asking for help.
i still need help with the last sentence.
now say something kind without another task.
you can see one part that is more clear than before.
write a longer story about a child hearing put them all away and asking which group all is about. use books and drawing paper.

a child had books and drawing paper across the table. his mother asked him to put them all away before dinner. he began carrying both the books and the paper to his room. she stopped him because the books were needed by another person coming soon. she had been looking at the paper when she spoke, but he had not seen where she was looking. they put the books back and made the request clear: put all the drawing paper away, but leave the books. he finished that task and asked whether the cup could stay too. this time, they said which thing they were talking about before choosing what should happen to it. all had not been the problem by itself. the question was which group it was about.
why did he move the books too?
he thought all was about everything on the table.
what did the mother want moved?
all the drawing paper, but not the books.
make the important idea of that story more simple.
they said which things they were talking about before choosing what to move.
can all be useful if the group is clear?
yes. all the drawing paper gives the group instead of making the child choose it from a look he did not see.
finish with the table ready for dinner.
he put the paper away and left the books on one side. then they made space for the meal on the rest of the table.
if i say the book might be on the shelf, do i know it is there?
no. might leaves it as a possible place, not a sure fact.
can that still help someone look?
yes. it can give a place to check while making clear that you are not sure.
write that as a message.
the book might be on the shelf, but i am not sure.
what if i just looked and saw it there?
then you can say: the book is on the shelf. i just saw it there.
does that mean it cannot move later?
no. it gives what you know now. someone could move it after that.
only give the message where i am not sure again.
the book might be on the shelf, but i am not sure.
write a longer story about someone saying a whole book is hard, then finding one kind of sentence is the real problem. keep the language simple.

a child put down a book and said it was too hard. his sister asked which part had stopped him. he showed her a long sentence with different parts about different days. the short sentences before it had been clear. they read the long one slowly and wrote what happened first, next, and last on another page. after that, he returned to the book and could follow the next part. he still wanted help with sentences like that one, but he no longer needed to call the whole book impossible. asking where the problem was had changed the help from reading everything for him to working on a specific part he could name.
what part had stopped him?
a long sentence with different parts about different days.
were all the sentences hard for him?
no. the short sentences before it were clear.
give the important idea of the story in one sentence.
they found one part that needed help and worked on it instead of calling the whole book impossible.
what question helped his sister understand the problem?
which part stopped you?
finish with him asking for help more clearly next time.
when another long sentence came, he showed it to her and asked about the order of the days.
i wrote morning but wanted to say afternoon. do not say my friend read the message wrong.
i wrote morning, but the time should be afternoon.
only give that message again.
i wrote morning, but the time should be afternoon.
can i add sorry?
sorry, i wrote morning, but the time should be afternoon.
why not say you did not understand me?
because your friend read the word you wrote. the problem was in your message, not in reading that word.
make that explanation shorter.
your friend used the word you gave. you can change the word without saying they read it wrong.
only give the message with sorry again.
sorry, i wrote morning, but the time should be afternoon.
there are six objects. i can see four, and two are inside a closed container. how many do i know the color of?
you may know the color of the four you can see, but you have not said whether you already know the color of the two inside.
why not just say four?
because you might already know about the two inside, even though you cannot see them now.
make that explanation shorter.
not seeing them now does not mean you never saw them before.
now i say i have never seen the two inside and nobody told me their color.
then you only have color information from the four outside, if you can see their color clearly.
only give the number i can see.
four.
can you know all six are the same color?
no. you have not given that detail.
i read before dinner. can i also say dinner was after my reading?
yes. those two sentences can give the same order: reading first, dinner later.
now change it so dinner is first.
i read after dinner.
can i keep before if i change the order of the two things?
yes. dinner was before my reading.
does changing the sentence order always change what happened first?
no. before and after help keep the time order clear even when the parts of the sentence change places.
only give two sentences about reading first.
i read before dinner. dinner was after my reading.
now only one about dinner first.
i read after dinner.
write a longer story about a child being asked where he reads. he should ask whether the person is asking about today or what he usually does.

a child was talking with his aunt about books. she asked where he read. he began saying that he was at school, then stopped because they had been talking about his reading at home. he asked whether she wanted to know where he read today or where he usually liked to read. she said she was asking about the place he usually read at home. he told her about a chair near the window. the answer at school could have been true for that day, but it would not have answered the question she had in mind. giving the time and kind of question made the conversation more clear without a long list of every place he had read before.
what two possible questions did he think of?
where he read today and where he usually read.
make that answer a sentence about what he asked.
he asked whether she wanted today or the place he usually read.
why was asking useful?
it kept him from giving a true answer to a different question.
write the child question in his own voice.
do you mean where i read today or where i usually read at home?
finish with him telling her about the chair.
he told her the chair was near the window, with a small table for his book and cup.
my friend asked good questions while i wrote. they did not write the story for me.
it sounds like their questions helped you choose your own words.
yes. one question was what do you want the person to do next.
that asks about the story you want, rather than giving you a different one.
make that reply shorter.
it leaves the next part for you to choose.
can you help me thank them for that specific kind of help?
thank you for asking questions that helped me find my own words.
does that say i wrote without any help?
no. it says what your friend did to help while keeping the words as your own.
make that explanation shorter.
you still wrote it, with help from their questions.
only give the thank you again.
thank you for asking questions that helped me find my own words.
say hello without choosing morning or evening.
hello. it is nice to hear from you.
now make it one word.
hello.
can you add my name if i have not given it?
no. i should ask or leave the name out rather than make one up.
only goodbye now.
goodbye.
is animal a wrong word if i know a more specific word?
not always. animal can be useful when the specific kind is not needed. a more specific word helps when you need that detail to understand the question.
make that explanation shorter.
the right detail is the one needed for the question.
what if i only want to say three animals came into the garden?
then animal may be enough. you can add what kind if it is important later.
can you know all three have the same needs from that word?
no. things in the same group can still be different from each other.
make that explanation shorter.
one group can have things with different needs.
only give a simple sentence about the group being different.
animals can have different needs.
i understand now. please do not say the whole answer again.
okay. i will leave it there.
just say something kind.
i hope it is useful for you.
now goodbye in two words.
take care.
only goodbye instead.
goodbye.
